name: kReturnErrorForUndefinedColumn
description: When set in the Query.flags field, the server returns an error if any column referenced in the query does not exist as a registered metric/attribute for the entity type. Without this flag, undefined columns are silently ignored. Set flags: 1 in your query to enable strict column validation.

name: kSkipGuidsForEmptyRawColumns
description: Optimizes count-only queries by skipping entity GUID fetching when no raw_columns are needed. When you only need aggregate counts (kCount) in a group_by and don't need per-entity rows, set flags: 2 to reduce memory and improve performance.

name: kForceMultiPhaseRawColumnFetch
description: Forces IDF to use a two-phase query strategy: first apply limit/sort to determine which entities match, then fetch the requested raw_columns only for those entities. This reduces memory when you have many columns but a small limit. Set flags: 4 to enable.

name: kFetchTotalUnfilteredEntityCount
description: Adds total_unfiltered_entity_count to the response, showing the total number of entities of that type BEFORE any where_clause filtering. Essential for building pagination UIs that show 'Showing 1-10 of 250 VMs'. Set flags: 16 in your query.

name: kSortByShardIds
description: Sorts query results by their internal shard IDs instead of the default ordering. Useful for deterministic iteration across all shards in a distributed IDF deployment. Set flags: 64 in your query.

name: kFetchTotalUnfilteredGroupCount
description: When using group_by queries, adds total_unfiltered_group_count to the response showing how many distinct groups exist before any having_clause or group_limit. Set flags: 128 to enable. Combine with kFetchTotalUnfilteredEntityCount (flags: 144 = 128+16) for both counts.

name: cursor_query_info (custom_expiration_time_secs)
description: Enables cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Set cursor_query_info.is_initial_cursor_query: true on the first call with a batch_size. The response returns next_cursor which you pass in subsequent calls. Use custom_expiration_time_secs to extend cursor lifetime beyond the default 30s (max controlled by insights_cursor_query_max_custom_expiration_time_secs = 120s).

name: Combined Flags (kForceMultiPhase + kFetchTotalCount)
description: Flags can be combined by adding their values. flags: 20 = kForceMultiPhaseRawColumnFetch (4) + kFetchTotalUnfilteredEntityCount (16). This gives you both optimized multi-phase fetching AND the total entity count in one query.

name: kForceSinglePhaseFetchContinuousGrouping
description: When using continuous (time-bucket) grouping, IDF normally does a pre-fetch phase to find min/max values for bucket boundaries. Set flags: 8 to skip this pre-fetch and force single-phase execution — useful when you already know the bucket boundaries or want faster response at the cost of less optimal bucketing.

name: Query.priority
description: Sets the processing priority for this query in the server's RPC queue. Lower values = higher priority. When the server is under load (controlled by insights_max_rpc_queue_time_secs = 30s and insights_max_queued_rpc_ops = 25), higher-priority queries are processed first. Critical queries should use priority: 0.

name: raw_limit with offset
description: Simple offset-based pagination using raw_limit { limit: N offset: M }. Skips M entities and returns the next N. Simpler than cursor queries but less efficient for deep pagination. The server gflag insights_fetch_shard_data_entity_limit (default: 3000) caps the maximum entities per shard that can be processed.
